title.narrative: Protection and Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) for IDP and Famine Response to Displacement and Famine in White Nile, Sudan.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe influx of IDPs in White Nile state since the outbreak of the conflict in 2023 has severely affected the availability of resources and services for the most vulnerable populations, including both internally displaced people (IDPs) and host communities. The state is experiencing shortages of food, clean water, health services, cash liquidity, shelter and other basic services such as non-food items (NFIs). The recent outbreak of conflict in Senna state has also led to an increase in the number of IDPs seeking refuge in White Nile. Over 136,000 people displaced from Senna have sought refuge in the state, according to IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM). Children are facing a wide range of protection risks including grave violations of human rights, separation from families, gender-based-violence (GBV) (particularly sexual violence and child marriage), trafficking, and limited access to child protection services. The Rapid Needs Assessment led by the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) in White Nile State, in July 2024 identified cash as the preferred transfer modality due to its ability to provide households with the flexibility and dignity to address their diverse priorities, such as food security, health, nutrition, protection, and WASH needs. ltbrgtThe consortium, led by Plan International Sudan (PIS), with Danish Refugee Council (DRC) and JASMAR, is launching an integrated Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) and protection intervention in Rabak and Kosti to address the ongoing challenges. PIS and DRC will implement the MPCA components in Rabak and Kosti respectively, while JASMAR will implement the protection component in both localities. The MPCA will provide essential cash transfers to help households meet their basic needs, such as food, hygiene products, and other essential needs, ensuring consistency across intervention areas through alignment with the Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB). Both programs will target families with children suffering from severe acute malnutrition (SAM), separated children, survivors of gender-based violence (GBV), and individuals with urgent protection concerns. The protection component, led by JASMAR, will provide case management services to unaccompanied and separated children (UASC), survivors of GBV, and persons with disabilities, as well as psychological support, counseling, and community awareness campaigns to promote resilience and prevent exploitation and abuse. JASMAR’s protection activities will also help to identify target beneficiaries for PIS and DRC’s in their MPCA programs. PIS and DRC will also refer protection cases to JASMAR for specialized services not covered by the MPCA. ltbrgtAdditionally, the project will integrate cross-cutting interventions in Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL), Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH), and Health and Nutrition. The consortium will collaborate with relevant clusters to monitor market conditions, adjust cash transfer values, and address hygiene-related needs, ensuring that interventions are responsive to the evolving situation. The consortium's active participation in national and regional humanitarian coordination bodies will ensure effective, coordinated interventions that maximize impact and avoid duplication.ltbrgtPIS will target 4,000 beneficiaries (700 HHs and 20 groups of 25 people) in Rabak and DRC will reach a total of 4,212 Beneficiaries (702 HHs) across Kosti locality. JASMAR will provide protection services to 3,630 individuals in both localities. These beneficiaries will receive integrated support through MPCA and protection services, with additional benefits from FSL, WASH, and Health and Nutrition interventions. This comprehensive approach aims to prevent acute malnutrition, reduce food insecurity, address protection cases, mitigate risks, and build long-term resilience among the most vulnerable populations in White Nile State, ultimately improving their ability to navigate the ongoing challenges posed by conflict in Sudan.ltbrgtlt/pgt
